cases.runtime_boundary: controlled topic generation through TopicScreeningScheduler receipt
cases.expected: Two workspaces with unrelated conflicting materials produce the same signed direction-first candidate family, research question, and semantic core without material leakage.

cases.runtime_boundary: controlled topic generation through TopicScreeningScheduler receipt
cases.expected: Changing only the direction contract while holding material constant changes both the direction digest and the signed candidate semantic core.

cases.runtime_boundary: TopicGenerationScheduler receipt for material_opportunity and workspace_extension
cases.expected: Explicit material-origin generation binds actual workspace-relative material text and SHA in its input digest, emits at least four substantive families, and becomes stale when the bound material changes.
A material-dependent candidate is accepted by the portfolio audit only under an explicitly declared material_opportunity origin; direction_first rejects the same dependency and generation lane.
Different titles with the same load-bearing semantic signature emit RDEC.PORTFOLIO.PSEUDO_DIVERSITY.

One candidate bypasses breadth only with attempted families, substantive elimination reasons and rationale, and an affirmative no-fabricated-companions declaration; removing or corrupting any element fails.
A candidate cannot replace its controller-signed seed lineage with an unsealed seed id.
The controlled screening scheduler refuses issuance unless every sealed seed receives exactly one retain, merge, or drop disposition.
A structurally valid topic, problem, contribution, and trajectory fit self-report cannot replace or contradict the controller-signed candidate core.
A post-screen material discovery must bind actual material text, path, SHA, direction, seeds, and screened cores; merely declaring the lane is rejected.

cases.runtime_boundary: selected-candidate subgraph plus localized material receipt validation
cases.expected: Material drift for a non-selected, non-critical discovery emits a local warning without staling the cleared selected candidate or its dependency subgraph.
